title: 528. The Nazis' Road to War: Hitler Prepares to Strike (Part 1)

sentences.en: Today, we are insulted.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们受到了侮辱。

sentences.en: Our blood brothers are at the mercy of their cruel abusers without any means of defending themselves.
sentences.zh: 我们的血肉同胞正任由他们残忍的虐待者摆布，却没有任何自卫的手段。

sentences.en: I am speaking of Czechoslovakia.
sentences.zh: 我所说的就是捷克斯洛伐克。

sentences.en: Among the suppressed minorities in this state are three and a half million Germans.
sentences.zh: 在这个国家受压迫的少数群体中，有三百五十万德国人。

sentences.en: These Germans are God's creatures.
sentences.zh: 这些德国人是上帝的子民。

sentences.en: The Almighty did not create them so that the Versailles Treaty could place them at the mercy of an alien power.
sentences.zh: 全能的上帝创造他们，并非为了让《凡尔赛条约》将他们置于异族权力的摆布之下。

sentences.en: And he did not create seven million Czechs to reign over these three and a half million, keep them in tutelage.
sentences.zh: 他创造七百万捷克人，也不是为了让他们统治这三百五十万人，将他们置于监护之下。

sentences.en: And far less did he create them for ravage and torture.
sentences.zh: 更不是为了让他们去蹂躏和折磨这些人。

sentences.en: The misery of the Sudeten Germans defies description.
sentences.zh: 苏台德地区德国人的苦难简直无法用语言形容。

sentences.en: They are being oppressed and humiliated in an unprecedented fashion.
sentences.zh: 他们正遭受着前所未有的压迫和羞辱。

sentences.en: There must be an end to the injustice inflicted upon these people.
sentences.zh: 这些人民所遭受的不公正待遇必须终结。

sentences.en: The Reich will no longer stand for any further oppression and persecutions of these three and a half million Germans.
sentences.zh: 德意志帝国绝不会再容忍对这三百五十万德国人的任何进一步压迫和迫害。

sentences.en: It is the duty of all of us to never again bow our heads to any alien will.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人的职责，就是永远不再向任何异族的意志低头。

sentences.en: To this, let us pledge ourselves.
sentences.zh: 让我们为此立誓。

sentences.en: So help us God.
sentences.zh: 愿上帝保佑我们。

sentences.en: So that, Dominic, was very much not a friend of the show, Adolf Hitler.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，刚才那段话的主人公阿道夫·希特勒，显然不是本节目的好朋友。

sentences.en: And he was speaking to the Nazi Party Congress in Nuremberg on the 12th of September 1938 about Czechoslovakia, as he frames it.
sentences.zh: 那是他在1938年9月12日的纽伦堡纳粹党代会上，就他所构想的捷克斯洛伐克问题发表的演讲。

sentences.en: And it's the beginning of the year.
sentences.zh: 现在是年初了。

sentences.en: We're into 2025 now.
sentences.zh: 我们已经进入2025年了。

sentences.en: And on the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 剩下的就是历史了。

sentences.en: If it's the new year, it must be Nazis.
sentences.zh: 如果是新年，那就一定是纳粹主题。

sentences.en: You're not wrong there, Tom.
sentences.zh: 你说得没错，汤姆。

sentences.en: That was a very spirited performance.
sentences.zh: 刚才那段表演真是充满激情。

sentences.en: You didn't do an accent, which is probably beSt.
sentences.zh: 你没有模仿口音，这大概是最好的选择。

sentences.en: I wanted to evoke the sense of Hitler through the power of my acting and my oratory.
sentences.zh: 我想通过我的表演和演讲力量来唤起人们对希特勒的感觉。

sentences.en: So I hope people got that sense.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望大家能感受到那种氛围。

sentences.en: If you do get cancelled for that reading, it's good to bow out in a very spirited performance.
sentences.zh: 如果你因为那段朗读而被“取消”了，能以如此激情的表演谢幕也算不错。

sentences.en: I also hope that people who may be watching this on YouTube will enjoy the hand gestures, which I thought were very Hitlerian.
sentences.zh: 我也希望在YouTube上观看的人能欣赏那些手势，我觉得非常有希特勒的风格。

sentences.en: They were very Hitlerian, yeah.
sentences.zh: 确实非常有希特勒的风格，没错。

sentences.en: And actually, the funny thing is, those are your usual hand gestures, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 说实话，有趣的是，那些不就是你平时常用的手势吗？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实是。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's actually how you speak off camera.
sentences.zh: 你私下说话时其实就是那样。

sentences.en: So actually, I find it quite easy.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说其实挺容易的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: So let's give people a bit of context.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们给听众提供一点背景信息。

sentences.en: What Hitler is doing there, obviously, is he is, on the face of it, defending the interests of the German-speaking minority in Western Czechoslovakia.
sentences.zh: 希特勒在那里所做的，表面上看，显然是在捍卫捷克斯洛伐克西部德语少数群体的利益。

sentences.en: People who, he says, have been ravaged and tortured by their Czech or Czechoslovakian overlords.
sentences.zh: 他说这些人一直受到捷克或捷克斯洛伐克统治者的蹂躏和折磨。

sentences.en: Of course, what he's really doing is preparing the ground for the invasion and dismemberment of Czechoslovakia,
sentences.zh: 当然，他真正做的是在为入侵和肢解捷克斯洛伐克做准备，

sentences.en: which he sees as a crucial step towards the creation of a new German dominion in Central and Eastern Europe.
sentences.zh: 他认为这是在欧洲中东部建立新德意志统治权的关键一步。

sentences.en: And Tom, as you said, we always like to welcome the New Year, the series about the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，正如你所说，我们总是喜欢以纳粹系列来迎接新年。

sentences.en: With the Third Reich.
sentences.zh: 以第三帝国为主题。

sentences.en: With the Third Reich.
sentences.zh: 以第三帝国为主题。

sentences.en: So we've done two series in the last couple of years.
sentences.zh: 过去几年我们已经做了两个系列了。

sentences.en: The first one was about their rise, the Nazis' rise to power in the 1920s up to 1933.
sentences.zh: 第一个系列是关于纳粹在20世纪20年代到1933年的崛起。

sentences.en: And the second one was about the Nazis and power in the course of the 30s.
sentences.zh: 第二个系列是关于纳粹在30年代的掌权。

sentences.en: And this one really will lead us up to the outbreak of the Second World War and the fall of Poland.
sentences.zh: 而这一系列将真正带我们走向第二次世界大战的爆发和波兰的沦陷。

sentences.en: And this week, we're going to be focusing on one of the most discussed, most controversial, most, I guess, genuinely infamous diplomatic episodes in history,
sentences.zh: 本周，我们将聚焦于历史上讨论最多、争议最大，我想也是真正最臭名昭著的外交事件之一，

sentences.en: which is the Munich Agreement of October 1938.
sentences.zh: 即1938年10月的《慕尼黑协定》。

sentences.en: I mean, I would say it's possibly the incident from history that has had the greatest influence on the way people, certainly people in the West,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这可能是历史上对人们——尤其是西方人——看待国际事务方式影响最大的事件，

sentences.en: have approached international affairs since the war.
sentences.zh: 自战争以来一直如此。

sentences.en: I mean, basically, it kind of lies behind everything from the Suez Crisis to the invasion of Iraq.
sentences.zh: 基本上，从苏伊士运河危机到入侵伊拉克，一切背后似乎都有它的影子。

sentences.en: It absolutely does.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: We don't want to be Neville Chamberlain.
sentences.zh: 我们不想成为内维尔·张伯伦。

sentences.en: We want to face down dictators.
sentences.zh: 我们想要对抗独裁者。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The Munich analogy is probably the most well-worn analogy, as you say, in all international relations.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，慕尼黑类比可能是所有国际关系中最陈词滥调的类比了。

sentences.en: And actually, I think it's a crisis that's generally a bit misunderstood and that the nuances of it are more surprising and more interesting than people think.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为这是一个普遍被误解的危机，其细微之处比人们想象的更令人惊讶、更有趣。

sentences.en: And maybe the lessons that people draw are not necessarily always the right ones.
sentences.zh: 也许人们从中得出的教训并不总是正确的。

sentences.en: So I think generally when people use the Munich analogy, they're using it merely as a political tool.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，通常当人们使用慕尼黑类比时，他们仅仅是把它当作一种政治工具。

sentences.en: As a justification to go to war.
sentences.zh: 作为发动战争的借口。

sentences.en: Justification for something they wanted to do anyway.
sentences.zh: 为他们无论如何都想做的事情寻找正当理由。

sentences.en: Of course, that's what politicians always do, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 当然，政客们总是这样，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We'll get into this in proper detail.
sentences.zh: 我们将详细探讨这一点。

sentences.en: And we'll start by, I think, by reminding ourselves how absolutely central the idea of war is to the whole Nazi project.
sentences.zh: 首先，我想我们要提醒自己，战争理念在整个纳粹计划中是多么核心。

sentences.en: So obviously, the first point, the foundational point, is that Nazism is driven above all by the shattering experience of the Great War and by the desire to put that right.
sentences.zh: 显然，第一点，也是基础点，纳粹主义主要是由大战（一战）带来的毁灭性经历以及纠正这一经历的渴望所驱动的。

sentences.en: So, as Ian Kershaw says, Richard Evans, all the great historians of Nazism and of Hitler,
sentences.zh: 正如伊恩·克肖、理查德·埃文斯以及所有研究纳粹主义和希特勒的伟大历史学家所言，

sentences.en: the single thing that drives it more than anything else is a sense of humiliation and a thirst for revenge after 1918.
sentences.zh: 驱动这一切的核心因素，莫过于1918年后的羞辱感和复仇渴望。

sentences.en: And actually, you don't need to be a Nazi to have that.
sentences.zh: 其实，你不需要成为纳粹也会有这种感觉。

sentences.en: So loads of people in Germany have that.
sentences.zh: 德国有很多人都有这种感觉。

sentences.en: Any conceivable nationalistic German leader in the 1930s or 1940s would probably have wanted to fight a war.
sentences.zh: 20世纪30年代或40年代任何可想而知的民族主义德国领导人，可能都会想要发动战争。

sentences.en: And so the Nazis come to power kind of in alliance with the conservative militaristic elites who had been, well, had been the elites, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以纳粹上台时，某种程度上是与保守的军国主义精英结盟的，这些人，嗯，一直是精英，你知道，

sentences.en: since the time of the Kaiser and before.
sentences.zh: 从德皇时代甚至更早开始。

sentences.en: And in 1938, are they still, they're still on the scene, right?
sentences.zh: 而在1938年，他们还在场，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, they've kind of been slightly sidelined, but they're still part of the makeup of the state.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们虽然被稍微边缘化了，但仍然是国家构成的一部分。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely they are.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And obviously in the army, there are lots of people in the army who've been there for years.
sentences.zh: 显然在军队里，有很多人已经在那里待了很多年了。

sentences.en: And Hitler's ambitions are absolutely, as they see it, in tune with their own longstanding ambitions that they've had since the day they were defeated in 1918,
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，希特勒的野心与他们自1918年战败以来长期持有的野心完全一致，

sentences.en: which is let's make Germany great again.
sentences.zh: 那就是让德国再次伟大。

sentences.en: Let's get our territory back.
sentences.zh: 让我们收复失地。

sentences.en: Let's expand our borders.
sentences.zh: 让我们扩张边界。

sentences.en: All of that.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But make Germany great again and get our borders back, but not necessarily should go into other countries that don't contain Germans and conquer them as well.
sentences.zh: 但是，让德国再次伟大并收复边界，并不一定意味着要进入没有德国人的其他国家并征服它们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And if Czechoslovakia contains a minority of Germans, then the majority are Czech and Slovaks.
sentences.zh: 如果捷克斯洛伐克包含少数德国人，那么多数人就是捷克人和斯洛伐克人。

sentences.en: And so that makes it slightly different, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这让情况变得有点不同，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Who've never been part of Germany.
sentences.zh: 他们从未成为德国的一部分。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So I think the point worth making is that Hitler, of course, is not an ordinary nationalistic politician.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为值得指出的是，希特勒当然不是一个普通的民族主义政客。

sentences.en: He's not like a lot of these other people.
sentences.zh: 他不像其他许多人那样。

sentences.en: So he has a very, very distinctive worldview, which we discussed at great length in the very first series we did.
sentences.zh: 他有着非常、非常独特的世界观，我们在第一个系列中已经深入讨论过了。

sentences.en: And at the center of it is this idea of racial struggle.
sentences.zh: 其核心是种族斗争的理念。

sentences.en: That comes from the social Darwinist ideas of the 1880s and 1890s.
sentences.zh: 这源于19世纪80年代和90年代的社会达尔文主义思想。

sentences.en: You know, you open the pages of Mein Kampf.
sentences.zh: 你知道，翻开《我的奋斗》的页面。

sentences.en: It's all full of this stuff about a coming race war, the struggle for the future of the planet.
sentences.zh: 里面全是关于即将到来的种族战争、关于地球未来的斗争的内容。

sentences.en: I mean, here's a random quotation.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这里有一个随机引语。

sentences.en: He who would live must fight.
sentences.zh: 想要生存的人就必须战斗。

sentences.en: He who does not wish to fight in this world where permanent struggle is the law of life does not have the right to exiSt.
sentences.zh: 在这个永恒斗争作为生命法则的世界里，不想战斗的人没有生存的权利。

sentences.en: Other European politicians do not talk like this in the 1920s and 1930s.
sentences.zh: 其他欧洲政客在20世纪20年代和30年代不会这样说话。

sentences.en: This is distinctive.
sentences.zh: 这是独特的。

sentences.en: You have to fight or you will be destroyed yourself.
sentences.zh: 你必须战斗，否则你就会被消灭。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: So I think it's fair to say that from the moment Hitler is propelled into office by those conservative elites in January 1933,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为可以公平地说，从希特勒在1933年1月被那些保守精英推上权力宝座的那一刻起，

sentences.en: absolutely everything is about preparing Germany for war.
sentences.zh: 绝对一切都是为了让德国为战争做准备。

sentences.en: War is not an accident.
sentences.zh: 战争不是意外。

sentences.en: War is the end goal.
sentences.zh: 战争是最终目标。

sentences.en: Richard Evans is brilliant on this in his book about the Nazis in power, about how everything that Hitler does is designed to make Germany racially fit for conflict.
sentences.zh: 理查德·埃文斯在他的《纳粹掌权》一书中对此有精彩的论述，关于希特勒所做的一切都是为了让德国在种族上适合冲突。

sentences.en: So that's everything from popular culture, from films and whatnot, all the way down to children's textbooks, by hammering this point home.
sentences.zh: 所以从流行文化、电影等等，一直到儿童教科书，都在不断灌输这一点。

sentences.en: Life is about struggle.
sentences.zh: 生命在于斗争。

sentences.en: The fittest will survive.
sentences.zh: 适者生存。

sentences.en: You have to be hard.
sentences.zh: 你必须坚强。

sentences.en: You have to be ruthless.
sentences.zh: 你必须冷酷无情。

sentences.en: There's a lot of PE, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 有很多体育课，不是吗？

sentences.en: There's an awful lot of PE, but there's a sort of a lot.
sentences.zh: 确实有大量的体育课，还有很多其他东西。

sentences.en: There's a moral re-education.
sentences.zh: 还有一种道德再教育。

sentences.en: You did a brilliant episode in our last series about the Nazis, about this kind of attempt to morally re-educate people, to brainwash people, I guess,
sentences.zh: 你在我们上一个关于纳粹的系列中做了一期精彩的节目，关于这种试图对人们进行道德再教育、我想是洗脑的尝试，

sentences.en: so that they become harder than hard.
sentences.zh: 让他们变得比坚硬更坚硬。

sentences.en: You know, the most ruthless people on the face of the planet.
sentences.zh: 你知道，成为地球上最冷酷无情的人。

sentences.en: Spartans.
sentences.zh: 斯巴达人。

sentences.en: Spartans, exactly, exactly.
sentences.zh: 斯巴达人，没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: So in pursuit of his goal, Hitler has been helped by three things.
sentences.zh: 所以为了实现他的目标，希特勒得到了三件事的帮助。

sentences.en: First of all, you've already mentioned it.
sentences.zh: 首先，你已经提到了。

sentences.en: He's had the support of the army and the conservative establishment because they're delighted by this.
sentences.zh: 他得到了军队和保守建制派的支持，因为他们对此感到欣喜若狂。

sentences.en: This is what they always wanted.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们一直想要的。

sentences.en: Secondly, he benefits from the fact that internationally, the Germans do actually have genuine sympathy.
sentences.zh: 其次，他受益于这样一个事实，即在国际上，德国确实获得了真正的同情。

sentences.en: There are loads of people in Britain and France who, for completely understandable reasons, you know, you may not agree with them now, but lots of people,
sentences.zh: 在英国和法国有很多人，出于完全可以理解的原因，你知道，你现在可能不同意他们，但很多人，

sentences.en: you can understand why they thought it.
sentences.zh: 你可以理解他们为什么会那样想。

sentences.en: People feel guilty about the Great War and the way that it ended.
sentences.zh: 人们对大战及其结束方式感到内疚。

sentences.en: They think it was a terrible struggle, slaughter.
sentences.zh: 他们认为那是一场可怕的斗争、一场屠杀。

sentences.en: Germany did lose a lot of territory.
sentences.zh: 德国确实失去了很多领土。

sentences.en: It did lose a lot of German speakers.
sentences.zh: 它确实失去了很多德语人口。

sentences.en: You know, who wouldn't be a bit upset about that?
sentences.zh: 你知道，谁会对此不感到难过呢？

sentences.en: Punic peace.
sentences.zh: 布匿式的和平。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Why shouldn't Germany have a proper army?
sentences.zh: 为什么德国不能拥有一支正规军？

sentences.en: Why shouldn't the Germans be treated with dignity and respect?
sentences.zh: 为什么德国人不能得到尊严和尊重？

sentences.en: So there are lots of people who think that.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多人是这样想的。

sentences.en: And then the third thing is because of the Great Depression, Britain and France in particular are fixated on their own internal problems, you know,
sentences.zh: 第三点是因为大萧条，英国和法国特别专注于他们自己的内部问题，你知道，

sentences.en: and they don't want to spend a lot of money on guns.
sentences.zh: 他们不想在武器上花很多钱。

sentences.en: They want to spend a lot of money on soup kitchens.
sentences.zh: 他们想在救济食堂上花很多钱。

sentences.en: So quite familiar.
sentences.zh: 所以很熟悉。

sentences.en: Yeah, yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: Very familiar.
sentences.zh: 非常熟悉。

sentences.en: So all of this meant that Hitler's foreign policy up to 1938 had actually been, if you're a conservative or nationalistic German, it's a succession of foreign policy,
sentences.zh: 所以这一切意味着，如果从保守或民族主义的德国人角度来看，希特勒到1938年为止的外交政策实际上是一连串的，

sentences.en: stunning achievements.
sentences.zh: 令人震惊的成就。

sentences.en: It takes them out of the League of Nations.
sentences.zh: 他带领他们退出了国际联盟。

sentences.en: You see massive rearmament, goes back into the Rhineland, which we did an episode about that, alliances with Italy and Japan, intervenes in the Spanish Civil War,

sentences.zh: 他肯定是花样滑冰界的托尼娅·哈丁。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's harsh on Tonya Harding, who's the subject of a very good film that made me more sympathetic to her.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这对托尼娅·哈丁来说太苛刻了，她可是那部非常棒的电影的主角，那部电影让我对她产生了更多同情。

sentences.en: Okay, well, fine.
sentences.zh: 好吧，行吧。

sentences.en: You can't equate Margot Robbie to Ribbentrop.
sentences.zh: 你不能把玛格特·罗比和里宾特洛甫相提并论。

sentences.en: No, that's strange casting.
sentences.zh: 不，那选角太奇怪了。

sentences.en: That's not casting anyone.
sentences.zh: 那根本不是在选角。

sentences.en: No, we want it put on the record.
sentences.zh: 不，我们想把它记录在案。

sentences.en: I think you should just say you're not comparing Ribbentrop to Margot Robbie.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你应该直接说你并没有把里宾特洛甫和玛格特·罗比做比较。

sentences.en: I'm not comparing Margot Robbie and Joachim from Ribbentrop.
sentences.zh: 我没有在比较玛格特·罗比和里宾特洛甫的约阿希姆。

sentences.en: I want to be quite clear about that.
sentences.zh: 我想把这一点说清楚。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: Okay, so Ribbentrop takes the hardest possible line at the foreign ministry.
sentences.zh: 好了，里宾特洛甫在外交部采取了最强硬的路线。

sentences.en: He always eggs Hitler on.
sentences.zh: 他总是怂恿希特勒。

sentences.en: He always says, you know, that's the way to Hitler's favour, basically, to be even more of a Nazi than Hitler is.
sentences.zh: 他总是说，你知道，这就是获得希特勒青睐的方法，基本上就是表现得比希特勒本人还要纳粹。

sentences.en: And secondly, I think this is a really important point.
sentences.zh: 其次，我认为这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: Ribbentrop is completely blinded by his hatred of Britain.
sentences.zh: 里宾特洛甫完全被他对英国的仇恨蒙蔽了双眼。

sentences.en: So he always says to Hitler, the British are absolutely spineless.
sentences.zh: 所以他总是对希特勒说，英国人完全没有骨气。

sentences.en: They are the most pathetic, pitiful curs.
sentences.zh: 他们是最可怜、最卑微的走狗。

sentences.en: They will never fight because they're too busy making jokes about champagne salesmen and Savile Row.
sentences.zh: 他们永远不会开战，因为他们忙着拿香槟推销员和萨维尔街开玩笑。

sentences.en: And if we do ever fight them, we will crush them like insects underfoot.
sentences.zh: 如果我们真的和他们打起来，我们会像踩死昆虫一样碾碎他们。

sentences.en: You know, so he really eggs it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所以他真的在煽风点火。

sentences.en: He gives Hitler very, very bad advice.
sentences.zh: 他给了希特勒非常、非常糟糕的建议。

sentences.en: And you know who else is, of course, revealing to Hitler that Britain's air defences aren't any good is Unity Mitford.
sentences.zh: 还有，当然，还有谁向希特勒透露英国的防空系统不行呢，那就是尤妮蒂·米特福德。

sentences.en: Yes, I wondered if she would make an appearance, an unwanted appearance in this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 是的，我还在想她会不会出现，以一种不受欢迎的方式出现在这个播客里。

sentences.en: And she has.
sentences.zh: 她确实出现了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So let's pick up the narrative in March 1938.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们从1938年3月开始讲起。

sentences.en: Hitler comes back from Vienna on the 15th of March to a tumultuous reception.
sentences.zh: 3月15日，希特勒从维也纳回来，受到了热烈的欢迎。

sentences.en: He's had an amazing time in Austria.
sentences.zh: 他在奥地利度过了一段美妙的时光。

sentences.en: He's been to his boyhood house.
sentences.zh: 他去了他儿时的故居。

sentences.en: He's addressed this enormous crowd.
sentences.zh: 他向那群庞大的人群发表了演讲。

sentences.en: And barely has he returned than he gets out a map.
sentences.zh: 他刚回来就拿出了地图。

sentences.en: Goebbels diary describes it and they go over the map together.
sentences.zh: 戈培尔的日记里描述了这件事，他们一起研究了地图。

sentences.en: And Hitler says, you know, I can't wait because basically I'm going to see.
sentences.zh: 希特勒说，你知道，我等不及了，因为基本上我将要看到。

sentences.en: I realize now that I will see in my lifetime the great German Reich, the German Empire over all Europe and all the world.
sentences.zh: 我现在意识到，我有生之年将会看到伟大的德意志帝国，那个统治整个欧洲乃至全世界的德意志帝国。

sentences.en: And the next step is going to be Czechoslovakia.
sentences.zh: 而下一步就是捷克斯洛伐克。

sentences.en: Because I'm right that with the Anschluss, so Austria is now part of a greater Reich, that Czechoslovakia is basically kind of sticking into the gut of this Reich.
sentences.zh: 因为我的判断是对的，随着德奥合并，奥地利现在成了大德意志帝国的一部分，而捷克斯洛伐克基本上就像是插在这个帝国腹部的一根刺。

sentences.en: So purely on a map, it looks like it should be swallowed up.
sentences.zh: 所以纯粹从地图上看，它看起来应该被吞并。

sentences.en: It's encircled.
sentences.zh: 它被包围了。

sentences.en: It's virtually encircled.
sentences.zh: 它几乎被包围了。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And it's a kind of island of Slavs surrounded by or partially surrounded by a lot of Germans.
sentences.zh: 它就像是一个被斯拉夫人组成的岛屿，被大量的德国人包围或部分包围着。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: However, Czechoslovakia is also a pretty serious target, a much more serious target than Austria.
sentences.zh: 然而，捷克斯洛伐克也是一个相当严肃的目标，比奥地利严肃得多。

sentences.en: It's bigger than Austria.
sentences.zh: 它比奥地利大。

sentences.en: It's got 15 million people.
sentences.zh: 它有1500万人口。

sentences.en: It was created from the Austro-Hungarian Empire.
sentences.zh: 它是由奥匈帝国分裂出来的。

sentences.en: So Bohemia and Moravia from the Austrian bit and Slovakia from the Hungarian bit.
sentences.zh: 波希米亚和摩拉维亚来自奥地利部分，斯洛伐克来自匈牙利部分。

sentences.en: It is by far the most sort of resilient liberal democracy in Central Europe.
sentences.zh: 它是中欧最坚韧的自由民主国家，没有之一。

sentences.en: It's got a very well-educated population.
sentences.zh: 它的人口受教育程度很高。

sentences.en: It has weathered the Depression reasonably well.
sentences.zh: 它相当平稳地度过了大萧条时期。

sentences.en: It's got a really, really serious industrial base.
sentences.zh: 它有着非常、非常雄厚的工业基础。

sentences.en: I mean, I know Skoda became a joke in Britain in the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我知道斯柯达在80年代的英国成了一个笑话。

sentences.en: Not in Northumberland.
sentences.zh: 在诺森伯兰郡可不是这样。

sentences.en: Not in Northumberland.
sentences.zh: 在诺森伯兰郡可不是这样。

sentences.en: Where everyone drives a Skoda Yeti.
sentences.zh: 那里每个人都开斯柯达Yeti。

sentences.en: Do they?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Sadie bought one.
sentences.zh: 萨迪买了一辆。

sentences.en: It's a pride and joy.
sentences.zh: 那是她的骄傲和快乐。

sentences.en: So we're very pro-Skoda.
sentences.zh: 所以我们非常支持斯柯达。

sentences.en: Golly.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: The other thing about Skoda...
sentences.zh: 关于斯柯达的另一件事……

sentences.en: Are you touting for sponsorship?
sentences.zh: 你是在拉赞助吗？

sentences.en: Is that what you're doing?
sentences.zh: 你是在做这个吗？

sentences.en: If Skoda want to give us a free Yeti, we're here.
sentences.zh: 如果斯柯达想送我们一辆免费的Yeti，我们随时欢迎。

sentences.en: But the other thing which I hadn't realised is that Skoda made the Bren gum, which I always thought was British.
sentences.zh: 但另一件我之前没意识到的是，斯柯达制造了布伦轻机枪，我一直以为那是英国造的。

sentences.en: Skoda is...
sentences.zh: 斯柯达是……

sentences.en: The Skoda Works, which is in Pilsen in Western Czechoslovakia, is one of the largest industrial complexes in Europe.
sentences.zh: 位于捷克斯洛伐克西部比尔森的斯柯达工厂，是欧洲最大的工业综合体之一。

sentences.en: It is a really, really serious business.
sentences.zh: 这真的是一家非常、非常严肃的企业。

sentences.en: So a massive prize for a German economy on its uppers.
sentences.zh: 所以对于处于困境中的德国经济来说，这是一个巨大的奖品。

sentences.en: It's a gigantic prize.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的奖品。

sentences.en: If you're playing a board game, you know, you're desperate to get this thing.
sentences.zh: 如果你在玩棋盘游戏，你知道，你会不惜一切代价得到它。

sentences.en: They make tanks.
sentences.zh: 他们制造坦克。

sentences.en: They make the best guns.
sentences.zh: 他们制造最好的枪支。

sentences.en: Some of the best guns in Europe.
sentences.zh: 欧洲最好的枪支之一。

sentences.en: Yeah, so the British Army are using it.
sentences.zh: 是啊，所以英国军队也在用它。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm amazed by that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我对此感到震惊。

sentences.en: They make tanks, tools, ships, locomotives.
sentences.zh: 他们制造坦克、工具、船只、火车头。

sentences.en: They've got lignite.
sentences.zh: 他们有褐煤。

sentences.en: They make loads and loads of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们制造各种各样的东西。

sentences.en: And Czechoslovakia therefore has this colossal military arsenal and a very, very well-trained and well-motivated army.
sentences.zh: 因此，捷克斯洛伐克拥有庞大的军事武库，以及一支训练有素、斗志昂扬的军队。

sentences.en: And Dominic, don't they also, on the borders where the kind of the mountains abut Germany, they've built a fairly impregnable series of defences.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，在那些山脉与德国接壤的边境线上，他们不是也建立了一系列相当坚不可摧的防御工事吗？

sentences.en: I mean, kind of Maginot line, but in a mountain chain.
sentences.zh: 我是说，类似于马奇诺防线，但在山脉中。

sentences.en: They have indeed.
sentences.zh: 他们确实建了。

sentences.en: Their frontier defences are pretty serious.
sentences.zh: 他们的边境防御相当严密。

sentences.en: They have a lot of raw materials.
sentences.zh: 他们有很多原材料。

sentences.en: They have tungsten.
sentences.zh: 他们有钨。

sentences.en: They have uranium ore, I think it is.
sentences.zh: 我想还有铀矿。

sentences.en: And Dominic, as I mentioned, lignite.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，正如我提到的，还有褐煤。

sentences.en: I don't really know what that is, but whenever I see it in this kind of book, I want the lignite.
sentences.zh: 我其实不知道那是什么，但每当我在这种书里看到它，我就想要褐煤。

sentences.en: And on top of that, the Czechs have two very serious allies.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，捷克人还有两个非常强大的盟友。

sentences.en: France, on the one hand, and the Soviet Union, on the other.
sentences.zh: 一个是法国，另一个是苏联。

sentences.en: And the fact that France is an ally, if France goes to war, then Britain is obliged to go to war.
sentences.zh: 而法国作为盟友的事实意味着，如果法国参战，那么英国就有义务参战。

sentences.en: Yeah, probably.
sentences.zh: 是的，大概吧。

sentences.en: And so we're back to a kind of pre-First World War.
sentences.zh: 所以我们又回到了第一次世界大战前的那种状态。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, mountaineers all tethered up by a single rope kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像登山者被一根绳子拴在一起的那种感觉。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So it's a tough nut to crack, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这是一块难啃的骨头，对吧？

sentences.en: On the other hand, if you could crack it, great, because these are the attractions.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，如果你能啃下它，那就太棒了，因为这些就是它的吸引力所在。

sentences.en: First of all, as you said, it's a rich Slav country that obtrudes into the Reich.
sentences.zh: 首先，正如你所说，这是一个深入帝国腹地的富裕斯拉夫国家。

sentences.en: So loads of Hitler's generals think, you know, I'd love to crush that.
sentences.zh: 所以很多希特勒的将军们会想，我真想把它碾碎。

sentences.en: It's allied to France.
sentences.zh: 它与法国结盟。

sentences.en: So if there is ever a war, Czechoslovakia would fight, and that would automatically mean Germany would face a war on two fronts.
sentences.zh: 所以如果发生战争，捷克斯洛伐克会参战，那自动意味着德国将面临两线作战。

sentences.en: So let's knock that out firSt.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们先把它解决掉。

sentences.en: That makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这说得通。

sentences.en: And am I right also that Hitler has potential allies himself because both the Hungarians and the Poles have kind of irredentist ambitions?
sentences.zh: 我说的对吗？希特勒自己也有潜在的盟友，因为匈牙利人和波兰人都有某种领土收复主义的野心？

sentences.en: They want to carve out a chunk.
sentences.zh: 他们想从中分一杯羹。

sentences.en: This is true of every country in Central Europe, and it will become a really important theme.
sentences.zh: 这是中欧每个国家的真实写照，这也将成为一个非常重要的主题。

sentences.en: So the dream of the French in particular was always to put together a kind of Central European alliance against Hitler.
sentences.zh: 所以法国人的梦想，特别是法国人，一直想建立一个针对希特勒的中欧联盟。

sentences.en: But the problem with that is exactly the point that you've identified, that their neighbors think, I quite fancy a bit of that.
sentences.zh: 但问题恰恰在于你指出的那一点，他们的邻居们想的是，我也想分一杯羹。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So that's going to be a real problem.
sentences.zh: 所以那将是一个真正的问题。

sentences.en: The Germans obviously want, as you've already mentioned, they want Czechoslovakia's raw materials.
sentences.zh: 德国人显然想要，正如你已经提到的，他们想要捷克斯洛伐克的原材料。

sentences.en: They want the industry.
sentences.zh: 他们想要工业。

sentences.en: They want the currency and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们想要货币之类的东西。

sentences.en: For Hitler, I think it's also quite personal.
sentences.zh: 对于希特勒来说，我认为这也很私人化。

sentences.en: He hates the Czechs, and he hates them because he was Austrian.
sentences.zh: 他讨厌捷克人，他讨厌他们是因为他是奥地利人。

sentences.en: And if you were a German-speaking Austrian before the First World War, the Czechs were basically your arch enemy within the empire.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一战前说德语的奥地利人，捷克人基本上就是你在帝国境内的死敌。

sentences.en: So they are the Slavs with whom Hitler had grown up kind of having a personal experience of.
sentences.zh: 所以他们是希特勒从小就有过亲身接触的斯拉夫人。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So not the Poles.
sentences.zh: 所以不是波兰人。

sentences.en: Not the Poles.
sentences.zh: 不是波兰人。

sentences.en: He has no – this will surprise people.
sentences.zh: 他没有——这会让人们感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Hitler has no kind of prior with the Poles.
sentences.zh: 希特勒和波兰人之间没有任何过往。

sentences.en: He doesn't care about the Poles.
sentences.zh: 他不在乎波兰人。

sentences.en: He's never had any dealings with them.
sentences.zh: 他从来没和他们打过交道。

sentences.en: For him, it's the Czechs.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，是捷克人。

sentences.en: But also he has a kind of artist's yearning to ride in triumph through Prague, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 而且他还有一种艺术家的渴望，想要凯旋穿过布拉格，不是吗？

sentences.en: This great, beautiful city with its incredible churches and, of course, synagogues.
sentences.zh: 这座宏伟、美丽的城市，有着令人难以置信的教堂，当然还有犹太会堂。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The great castle.
sentences.zh: 那座伟大的城堡。

sentences.en: So a bit like Paris, I guess.
sentences.zh: 所以我想有点像巴黎吧。

sentences.en: It kind of haunts his imagination as a foreign city that he would love to have as a prize.
sentences.zh: 它就像一座他渴望作为战利品拥有的外国城市，萦绕在他的想象中。

sentences.en: He has that sort of slightly adolescent, Wagner-loving fantasy.
sentences.zh: 他有一种那种略带青春期、热爱瓦格纳的幻想。

sentences.en: I will ride through Prague as a conqueror.
sentences.zh: 我要以征服者的身份穿过布拉格。

sentences.en: You know, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是那种感觉。

sentences.en: He absolutely has it.
sentences.zh: 他绝对有这种想法。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So as Lug would have it, going back to the speech that you began in the episode, he has a perfect pretext for German action.
sentences.zh: 所以正如卢格所说，回到你在本集开头提到的演讲，他有了一个完美的德国行动借口。

sentences.en: Because the great flaw of Woodrow Wilson's project after the First World War of self-determination and all these new nation states was there are so many minorities.
sentences.zh: 因为伍德罗·威尔逊在第一次世界大战后提出的民族自决和所有这些新民族国家的计划，其最大的缺陷就是有太多的少数民族。

sentences.en: And in Czechoslovakia, there are three million German speakers who live along the western border, this area known as the Sudetenland.
sentences.zh: 而在捷克斯洛伐克，有三百万德语人口居住在西部边境，这个地区被称为苏台德地区。

sentences.en: Now, they have never been Germans.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他们从来都不是德国人。

sentences.en: They were Austrian subjects.
sentences.zh: 他们是奥地利的臣民。

sentences.en: But obviously, in this world of nationalism, of new nation states, their German-ness, the fact they speak German, becomes a massive issue for them.
sentences.zh: 但很显然，在这个民族主义和新兴民族国家林立的世界里，他们的“德国属性”，即他们说德语这一事实，对他们而言成了一个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: Now, they are pretty well treated.
sentences.zh: 目前，他们受到的待遇相当不错。

sentences.en: They're probably better treated than any other minority in Europe.
sentences.zh: 他们受到的待遇可能比欧洲任何其他少数族裔都要好。

sentences.en: They have full legal equality with their Czech neighbours.
sentences.zh: 他们在法律上与捷克邻居享有完全平等的地位。

sentences.en: They're pretty well.
sentences.zh: 他们过得还不错。

sentences.en: You know, the Czechs don't massively discriminate against them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，捷克人并没有大规模地歧视他们。

sentences.en: But they've been quite hard hit by the Depression.
sentences.zh: 但他们受大萧条的打击相当严重。

sentences.en: So a lot of them have been put out of work.
sentences.zh: 所以他们当中很多人失业了。

sentences.en: And secondly, of course, over the border, they've got this bloke ranting and raving about Germandom and saying he's going to build a greater German Reich.
sentences.zh: 其次，当然，在边境那边，有个家伙正大肆鼓吹“德意志性”，声称要建立一个大德意志帝国。

sentences.en: So obviously, a lot of them think, I fancy being part of that.
sentences.zh: 所以很显然，他们当中很多人心想，我倒是想成为其中的一部分。

sentences.en: And the main Sudeten German party is led by this bloke who was an Austrian war veteran called Konrad Henlein, who also, I have to say, was a gymnastics instructor.
sentences.zh: 苏台德德意志党的主要领导人是那个叫康拉德·亨莱因的家伙，他是一位奥地利战争老兵，而且我必须得说，他还是个体操教练。

sentences.en: And I think he's a PE teacher.

sentences.en: And he says, oh, let's, you know, let's basically get into bed with Hitler.
sentences.zh: 他说，噢，咱们，你知道，咱们干脆跟希特勒穿一条裤子吧。

sentences.en: So Hitler, as soon as he gets back from the Anschluss, he sets the wheels in motion.
sentences.zh: 所以希特勒一从德奥合并回来，就开始着手行动了。

sentences.en: He gets Henlein to Berlin for a secret meeting and he says, right, I want to sort this out.
sentences.zh: 他把亨莱因召到柏林进行秘密会谈，并说，好了，我想解决这个问题。

sentences.en: Like, I'm going to start agitating for you.
sentences.zh: 就像是，我要开始为你煽动舆论了。

sentences.en: Let's get you all riled up.
sentences.zh: 让我们把你们都煽动起来。

sentences.en: So a month later, April 1938, Henlein gets his party together and he says, oh, we're being totally bullied by the Czechs.
sentences.zh: 一个月后，即1938年4月，亨莱因召集了他的党徒，说，噢，我们正受到捷克人的全面欺凌。

sentences.en: We want total self-government.
sentences.zh: 我们要完全的自治。

sentences.en: Now, the important thing here is they don't.

sentences.en: This is not the aim.
sentences.zh: 这并不是他们的目标。

sentences.en: The aim is actually to dismember the whole of Czechoslovakia.

sentences.en: This is just a pretext.
sentences.zh: 这只是个借口。

sentences.en: So Czechoslovakia said, oh, brilliant.

sentences.zh: 好吧，你们可以自治。

sentences.en: That's not good enough.

sentences.en: That's not what they want.

sentences.en: They want to make that.

sentences.zh: 他们想给捷克人提出一堆他们根本无法满足的要求。

sentences.en: So make them so humiliating that there's no way that the Czech government can possibly accept them.
sentences.zh: 所以要让这些要求变得极其羞辱，以至于捷克政府根本不可能接受。

sentences.en: A little bit like that Austrian ultimatum to Serbia before the First World War.

sentences.en: Again, worth emphasizing, this is not just about the Sudetenland.
sentences.zh: 再次强调，这不仅仅是为了苏台德地区。

sentences.en: He wants the whole country.
sentences.zh: 他想要整个国家。

sentences.en: He says to the head of the Wehrmacht, a guy called Wilhelm Keitel, he says, I want the whole country as a launch pad for the showdown in the East with Bolshevism.
sentences.zh: 他对国防军总司令威廉·凯特尔说，我想要整个国家作为在东方与布尔什维克进行决战的跳板。

sentences.en: So he's still thinking beyond this, right?
sentences.zh: 所以他还在考虑更长远的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: Again, fighting the USSR.

sentences.en: And he also says, when we do invade, I want the whole thing done and dusted in four days because I don't want to give the British and the French,
sentences.zh: 他还说，当我们入侵时，我希望在四天内彻底解决战斗，因为我不想给英国人和法国人……

sentences.en: I want to present them with a fait accompli so that they don't get stuck in as well.

sentences.en: But at this point, he says, this is a long term thing.

sentences.en: We're not going to rush this.

sentences.en: This could be like a year, a couple of years.

sentences.en: Who knows?

sentences.en: At the same time, the Germans army are having maneuvers, just ordinary kind of military maneuvers, nothing sinister in it.

sentences.en: And as a result of this, there's all sorts of sort of diplomatic excitement, rows between ambassadors and stuff.

sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 他因为威望受损而感到愤怒。

sentences.zh: 他召集了他的将军们。
